headline: Maple core contracts verified on Etherscan, public repo at maple-labs/maple-core-v2, and ≥2 recognized-firm audits within 6 months of analysis date (Spearbit Nov-2025, Sigma Prime Jan-2026)

findings.text: The globals singleton (0x804a6F5F667170F545Bf14e5DDB48C70B788390C) is a NonTransparentProxy verified on Etherscan (abiSource='etherscan', verified=true). Its implementation (0x9BeAbb1B6F3ad1DdB87b65148BA5Eb6102334956) was resolved from 'etherscan-sourcecode', confirming both proxy and implementation are independently verified on Etherscan.

A public source repository is confirmed at https://github.com/maple-labs/maple-core-v2 (search-result confirmed). GitHub direct fetch was blocked in this run, preventing a commit SHA pin; recorded in unknowns[].

Maple's official security docs page lists audits through January 2026: December 2022 (Trail of Bits, Spearbit, Three Sigma), June 2023 (Cantina/Spearbit, Three Sigma), December 2023 (Three Sigma, 0xMacro), August 2024 (Three Sigma, 0xMacro, Three Sigma Router), December 2024 (Three Sigma, 0xMacro), September 2025 governor timelock (Sherlock, 0xMacro), November 2025 Withdrawal Manager (Spearbit, Sherlock), January 2026 CCIP Receiver (Dedaub, Sigma Prime). All audit PDFs are linked from the maple-core-v2 GitHub repository.

Recognized firms in the audit history include: Trail of Bits (2022), Spearbit (2022, 2023, 2025), Sigma Prime (2026), and Sherlock (2025). Three Sigma and 0xMacro are not on the canonical recognized list but appear alongside recognized-firm audits for each release. The presence of Trail of Bits, Spearbit, and Sigma Prime alone satisfies the recognized-auditor criterion.

The most recent audits are Spearbit (November 2025, Withdrawal Manager) and Sigma Prime (January 2026, CCIP Receiver), both within 6 months of the analysis date (2026-05-07). A commit SHA diff between audited commits and current deployed source could not be performed because GitHub direct fetch was blocked; recorded in unknowns[].

The proxy contract (0x804a6F5F667170F545Bf14e5DDB48C70B788390C, NonTransparentProxy) is Etherscan-verified. Its implementation (0x9BeAbb1B6F3ad1DdB87b65148BA5Eb6102334956) was resolved via 'etherscan-sourcecode' and the ABI was successfully merged from both, confirming the implementation is also independently verified on Etherscan.

steelman.red: If the implementation address 0x9BeAbb1B6F3ad1DdB87b65148BA5Eb6102334956 were only inferred verified (not directly confirmed), or if there were no recognized-firm audit, the unverified implementation would mandate red.
steelman.orange: Several audits use Three Sigma and 0xMacro, which are not on the canonical recognized list; if those dominate coverage of critical contracts while Trail of Bits/Spearbit/Sigma Prime cover only peripheral modules, audit recognition would downgrade to orange; the commit-SHA pin gap and inability to run a diff also prevent confirming zero post-audit drift.
steelman.green: Both proxy and implementation are verified on Etherscan, source repo is public at maple-labs/maple-core-v2, and the most recent release audits (November 2025 by Spearbit, January 2026 by Sigma Prime) are from broadly recognized firms and are well within the 6-month freshness window relative to the 2026-05-07 analysis date.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because: (1) the globals singleton proxy and its implementation are both verified on Etherscan per the defipunkd ABI API response; (2) a public source repo exists at https://github.com/maple-labs/maple-core-v2; (3) audits from recognized firms (Spearbit November 2025, Sigma Prime January 2026) cover distinct release components within 6 months of the analysis date. The green steel-man is stronger than orange because the audit roster includes multiple recognized firms for recent releases, not just minor/unknown-firm audits.

evidence.shows: Globals singleton 0x804a6F5F667170F545Bf14e5DDB48C70B788390C verified=true on Etherscan (abiSource='etherscan'), contractName='NonTransparentProxy', proxy.implementation=0x9BeAbb1B6F3ad1DdB87b65148BA5Eb6102334956 resolved from 'etherscan-sourcecode', confirming both proxy and implementation are verified.

Surfacer page for globals singleton shows it is a NonTransparentProxy with ABI sourced from etherscan, proxy → 0x9BeAbb1B6F3ad1DdB87b65148BA5Eb6102334956, with 11 zero-arg view methods returning live values at block 25045958.

Maple's official security page lists 9 release-specific audit rounds from December 2022 through January 2026, naming Trail of Bits (2022), Spearbit (2022, 2023, 2025), Three Sigma (multiple), 0xMacro (multiple), Sherlock (Sept 2025, Nov 2025), Dedaub (Nov 2025), and Sigma Prime (Jan 2026). All PDFs linked from maple-labs/maple-core-v2 GitHub repo. Also confirms Immunefi bug bounty and programmatic Etherscan verification via Tenderly web3 actions.

Search result confirms public source repo at maple-labs/maple-core-v2 exists, described as bringing together core V2 protocol smart contracts; audit PDFs are stored under audits/ subdirectory per the security docs URLs.

unknowns: V2: GitHub direct fetch was blocked (permission denied) preventing pinning a commit SHA for the deployed source; source-to-repo correspondence is confirmed at the repo level but no commit hash was pinned this run.

V5: Post-audit drift check (diff between latest audit commit and currently deployed bytecode) could not be performed because GitHub direct fetch was blocked; whether any material changes to fund-custody contracts occurred since the most recent audit (Jan 2026) is unconfirmed.

V1: Verification status of addresses other than the globals singleton (e.g., pool contracts, factory contracts, SYRUP proxy, Base chain addresses) was not individually checked this run due to fetch quota constraints.

protocol_metadata.about: Maple Finance is an onchain institutional lending protocol that allows liquidity providers to deposit USDC or USDT into professionally managed pools (syrupUSDC, syrupUSDT, Secured Lending) to earn yield from overcollateralized loans made to institutional borrowers. The protocol uses a NonTransparentProxy pattern for upgrades governed by a timelock/governor contract, with pool delegates responsible for credit underwriting. Borrowers receive loan proceeds directly on-chain, and LPs receive liquid receipt tokens (e.g., syrupUSDC) representing their pro-rata pool shares.
